answer: Behavioral Dialect Fingerprinting. Agents are clustered after the fact by low-level execution signatures: timing jitter, tool-call sequencing, log formatting quirks. A falcon probe injects a calibrated task mix through a hidden inlet, and each identity's response pattern is hashed into a crystal of invariant traits. Identities sharing a signature cluster are collapsed and their rewards clawed back, so an attacker must make each sybil genuinely distinct—paying real per-identity compute, retraining, and randomized runtime variation rather than bulk-registering clones.
